Commentary.Commentary: We have some bad news for you. It's been raining continuously in Sharjah and the conditions are unsuitable for any kind of game. The match has been ABONDONED officially due to torrential downpour. Do join us for the third and final game. Afghanistan have a lead but Ireland would look to square the series. Join us on 12th of this month at 5pm IST (11.30 am GMT) Till then, cheers!

We are down to the second ODI between Afghanistan and Ireland at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium. It was an absolute run-fest in the series opener, where the Afghans emerged victorious to take the lead. Hashmatullah Shahidi and his men would want to seal the series with a game to go, whereas Paul Stirling's Ireland will look to hit back and force a series decider. After being inserted into bat, Rahmanullah Gurbaz's 6th ODI ton and contributions from Ibrahim Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, and Hashmatullah Shahidi took the hosts to 310. In reply, Ireland made a good fist of it thanks to the partnership between Harry Tector and Lorcan Tucker. However, once this stand was broken, it left the rest of the batting unit with too much to do. As the Irish strive to bounce back, responsibility will fall on their top order, consisting of Paul Stirling, Andy Balbirnie, and Curtis Campher who failed to have any sort of impact in the first game. Lorcan Tucker and the centurion from the last game, Harry Tector, will be pivotal again in holding the Irish inning together. On the bowling front, left-arm spinner Theo van Woerkom was the shining light for them. The spearhead of the pace attack, Mark Adair, went wicketless, and the visitors will require him, Andy McBrine, and Craig Young to step up if they are to keep the series alive. As far as Afghanistan are concerned, their ace speedster Fazalhaq Farooqi was sensational upfront and at the death as well, leading the charge. As the hosts aim to wrap up the series, they will be hoping for better results with the ball from the likes of Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib, and Noor Ahmad. It was a near-perfect day for the Afghan batters on what was a slow and low surface, and they will look to take the momentum into this game. The onus will be on Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran to provide a strong start, while Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib, and Azmatullah Omarzai will have to fire on all cylinders towards the back end of the innings. It was Afghanistan's fifth win on the trot against Ireland in ODI cricket, and they will look to extend their dominance and seal the series. Will they succeed in doing so? Or will it be Ireland to take the series to a decider? We shall find out.
